previous_evidence: Section 2.1 average weekday curve decreases at 12 and increases at 13. Existing E018 compares 15-minute boundary values, so its rates cannot be substituted here.
question: Does the hourly-mean shape occur on actual dates, separately for weekdays and weekends?
scope: Jan-Aug, 5784 valid hours / 241 dates. Weekday 171, weekend 70, public holidays included by weekday. Gray calendar rows are invalid July 13 and July 15, not zero power.
confirmed: Strict M12<M11 and M13>M12: weekday 147/171 (85.96%), weekend 13/70 (18.57%). Counts include small changes; direction and magnitude must be read together.
Median paired changes 11->12 / 12->13: weekday -64 / +61, weekend -1 / 0. These are medians of per-date changes, not differences between hourly medians.
Weekday nonmatching dates: 24 total, including 20 with no positive production record all day. Positive-production weekday matches 145/149 (97.32%); all-zero-production weekday matches 2/22 (9.09%).
Weekend positive-production matches 6/32 (18.75%); all-zero-production matches 7/38 (18.42%). Production presence alone does not explain calendar differences.

Full 96-slot profiles repeat. One vote per distinct profile within each calendar group: weekday 78/90 (86.67%), weekend 12/47 (25.53%). Groups may share a profile, so group distinct counts are not additive. No records were deleted.
Among matching weekdays, 13-hour average reaches the 11-hour average in only 51/147. Rebound does not generally mean full recovery.
The daily lines show wide day-to-day variation on weekends and a sizable mean/median difference. A single average curve is insufficient to describe every date.
judgment_update: 2.1's weekday midday dip/rebound is observed on most individual weekdays, especially those with positive production. It is not a universal calendar rule. Weekends mix different trajectories and levels. Normal schedule, lunch break, equipment use and true shutdown causes remain unidentified.
next_or_stop: The approved question has been answered, including exceptions by month and production presence, plus repeated-profile sensitivity. Stop this descriptive iteration. Future use of calendar/history inputs needs modeling validation; this EDA does not demonstrate prediction performance. Hourly-average versus four-slot variation is a separate planned 2.4 question and has not been executed here.
